newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks to revive stalled budget process.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks to revive stalled budget process.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's overture to Congress Tuesday on balancing the budget reflects his embrace of public comments by top Republicans, rather than any progress in private talks, a senior official said.

"I don't think we are referring to anything that might have been said privately," said the senior administration official, who asked not to be identified. "We're referring to public comments by the Speaker and Senator Lott."
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Speaker of the House of Representatives Newt Gingrich endorsed the idea of putting off a major tax cut in order to reach a balanced budget deal.
Separately, Republican Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott suggested on Monday he was flexible on the key question of whose economic assumptions to use in the budget talks.

Seizing on their remarks, Clinton on Tuesday invited the leaders of the congressional budget committees to meet him on Wednesday to discuss the budget before he leaves for a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

Since Clinton proposed his balanced budget plan six weeks ago, there has been no progress on an agreement in talks with the Republican-controlled Congress, and even his own officials admit that matters are stymied.
While deploring the partisanship that led to his first choice to be Director of the CIA, Anthony Lake, withdrawing his nomination on Monday, Clinton sought to turn that reverse to his advantage.

"The cycle of political destruction must end," he said. "We can't let partisan bickering stop us from doing the work we were sent here to do ... We have to seize this opportunity to pass a bipartisan agreement to balance the budget."
The administration official rejected the argument that Clinton was simply engaging in theatrics.
"The president is trying to energize a process that has not yet had that much energy to it," said the official.

"If it requires him to make a series of public appearances for the explicit purpose of keeping momentum going, building momentum, re-energizing the process, so be it," he added. "Is it only theater? No."
